chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie and Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Hanan ibn Sadeer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a Muslim man who was immoral with a Jewish woman, so she gave birth to a child. Then he died and did not leave any inheritors. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The inheritance is handed over to his child from the Jewish woman.'

I said: 'And what about a Christian man who was immoral with a Muslim woman, so she gave birth to a boy, then the Christian man died and left wealth; for whom would be his inheritance?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His inheritance would be for his son from the Muslim woman.'

key_terms.فَجَرَ: To be immoral or commit fornication/illicit sexual act

ai.seo_question: Who inherits from a man who has a child with a non-Muslim woman through illicit relations?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'nasab' (lineage) in Shia jurisprudence, establishing that a child born from illicit relations (fujur) with a non-Muslim woman retains inheritance rights from the father, provided the father is Muslim. It highlights the distinction between the mother's religion and the child's eligibility to inherit from the paternal line, reinforcing the legal status of the 'walad al-fujur' in property distribution.
